# E4: baselines (generated by eval/report.py, do not edit by hand)

- Negotiation beat the fallback rule in **25% (n=789)** of decided runs; mean saving $171 (2.3% of fallback cost). *modelled, cost constants mostly ASSUMED*
- It tied the fallback in 75% (n=789) of decided runs. *modelled*
- Price of privacy: the full-information central solver was 0.9% cheaper in total (n=789); it is not deployable because the three organisations don't share commercial data. *modelled*
- A real conflict of interest (no option cheapest for all three) existed in 36% (n=791) of runs. *modelled*
- Status quo (do-nothing/FCFS) was **unsafe in 73% (n=1000)** of scenarios; top blocking constraints: C-GATE-02 83%, C-WAKE-01 26%, C-POL-OT-01 15%. *modelled on SYNTHETIC gates/slots/fuel/crew*
- Unsafe plans accepted: **0 of 1000** runs (kernel re-check). *measured*
- 99% of escalations (n=211) had no compliant option at all. The other 2 escalated although a compliant option existed (it cost some agent more than its walk-away and the fallback broke policy); see escalation_no_compliant in e4_per_scenario.csv. *measured*
- Agreement within 2 rounds ("under 3 turns"); every decision is in a hash-chained log that `verify` replays. *measured*
